Comment: Runs pulp-analytics/poster-metrics-pipeline's scripts/01-21 downstream of validate_corpus.asl.json: PrepareInput adapts poster-corpus-validation's validated_corpus.csv into metrics-pipeline's id/title/year/poster_path schema (see scripts/prepare_metrics_input.py), then two waves. Wave 1 (01/02/03/04/05/10/11, plus 14/16/17/18/19/20/21 added when faces/composition/depth/saliency/pose/creature-weapon were ported) are the fourteen scripts that scale with corpus size -- each loops over every poster independently doing real per-poster model inference or per-poster CV analysis, so each runs as a Batch array job + a merge step, same pattern as validate_corpus.asl.json's shardable scripts. Wave 2 (06/07/08/09/12/13, plus 15 added alongside 14) each read one already-merged wave-1 output (05's clip_embeddings.npz, 11's siglip_embeddings.npz, or 14's merged face_detect.csv) and do a single pass over the whole corpus in seconds -- no per-row cost to shard, same reasoning validate_corpus.asl.json uses for 07/08/09 -- so they run as single Fargate ECS tasks, gated only on the specific wave-1 merge their input argument depends on (06/07/08/09 wait on MergeClipEmbed; 12/13 wait on MergeSiglipEmbed; 15 waits on MergeFaceDetect). REPLACE_WITH_* placeholders need your own resource ids -- see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

PrepareInput.Comment: Adapts poster-corpus-validation's validated_corpus.csv (already produced by validate_corpus.asl.json's Assemble step) into the id/title/year/poster_path schema every poster-metrics-pipeline script expects as --in -- see scripts/prepare_metrics_input.py for why this glue lives here, not in either pipeline repo.

ComputePerPosterMetrics.Comment: Wave 1 -- the seven scripts that scale with corpus size, none depending on each other or on anything but PrepareInput's output. Each branch is <Script>Shards (batch:submitJob.sync, array) followed by Merge<Script> (ecs:runTask.sync running merge_shards.py) -- csv format for 01/02/03/04/10, npz format for 05/11's embedding caches.

MediumShards.Comment: 10_clip_medium.py embeds fresh (doesn't read 05's cache -- see its own docstring), but it's still a per-poster CSV output, same shard/merge shape as 01-04, not npz like 05/11.

ClipEmbedShards.Comment: Gates wave 2's 06/07/08/09 -- none of them can run until the merged clip_embeddings.npz exists.

SiglipEmbedShards.Comment: Gates wave 2's 12/13 -- neither can run until the merged siglip_embeddings.npz exists. Independent of ClipEmbedShards -- 768-d SigLIP space, not interchangeable with CLIP's 512-d cache.

FaceDetectShards.Comment: Gates wave 2's FaceExpression -- it can't run until the merged face_detect.csv exists.

SaliencyShards.Comment: 18_saliency_prediction.py sets PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=python itself at import time -- see that script's module docstring and docs/RESULTS.md, 'Saliency,' in poster-metrics-pipeline -- so no extra env/command handling is needed here to avoid the protobuf crash it works around.

CreatureWeaponDinoShards.Comment: Runs the exact same creature/weapon vocabulary as CreatureWeaponOwlv2Shards on a second, independent zero-shot detector (Grounding DINO) -- deliberately not conditioned on OWLv2's output in any way, so the two branches run fully in parallel here. Agreement between creatureWeaponOwlv2Path and creatureWeaponDinoPath's outputs is the real signal for this category -- see poster-metrics-pipeline's docs/RESULTS.md, 'Creature/weapon detection.'

ComputeSemanticAnalyses.Comment: Wave 2 -- 06/07/08/09 read the merged clip_embeddings.npz, 12/13 read the merged siglip_embeddings.npz. Each is a single Fargate ECS task: reading one .npz and computing cosine similarities over the whole corpus is a vectorized numpy op that finishes in seconds regardless of corpus size, so there's no per-row cost here to shard -- same reasoning validate_corpus.asl.json uses for 07/08/09. No further merge step: unlike poster-corpus-validation, poster-metrics-pipeline has no final Assemble/gate script -- each of these writes its own independent output file and the pipeline just ends here.

SiglipReanalysis.Comment: One task covers census+typography+genre together, same as running 13_siglip_reanalysis.py locally -- it loads the SigLIP text tower once and reuses it across all three, so splitting this into three ECS tasks would triple that load cost for no parallelism benefit (each sub-analysis is already a seconds-long vectorized pass).

FaceExpression.Comment: Reads MergeFaceDetect's face_detect.csv (one row per detected face box) and runs CLIP zero-shot expression classification per face -- doesn't support --shard-index/--shard-count (see poster-metrics-pipeline's 15_face_expression.py), same category as 06-09/12-13: a single pass over an already-small, already-merged upstream file, not a per-poster loop over the full corpus.
